subject: Unable to recover parameters from simulated data by growth curve modeling

messages.author: b7262ee995154b25
messages.subject: Unable to recover parameters from simulated data by growth curve modeling
parts:
Hello everyone,

i just encountered a problem with the estimation of the parameters, that i used to simulate some time series data.
the growth curve ist essentially driven by three random variables: (a) an intercept, (b) a slope, and (c) a factor called 'pulse', that has nonlinear loadings with respect to time:

#generate data
N <- 200
id <- 1:N
intercept <- rnorm(N,2,.5)
slope <- rnorm(N,-.18,.01)
pulse <- rnorm(N,.9,.3)

t0 <- init + pulse*0.00 + decay*0
t1 <- init + pulse*1.00 + decay*2
t2 <- init + pulse*0.51 + decay*3
t3 <- init + pulse*0.15 + decay*4
t4 <- init + pulse*0.04 + decay*5
t5 <- init + pulse*0.00 + decay*6
simdat <- data.frame(id,t0,t1,t2,t3,t4,t5)

this data was supposed to illustrate the concept of latent time scaling, i.e. the loadings of the nonlinear pulse factor (except for the first and the second) are be estimated from the data.
unfortunately this did not work as expected. even if the loadings of this factor were contrained to their a-priori known values, lavaan either returned an error message like "unable to invert sample cov-matrix", or just some arbitrary estimates and a really bad model fit:

mod <- "
t0 ~~ e0*t0
t1 ~~ e1*t1
t2 ~~ e2*t2
t3 ~~ e3*t3
t4 ~~ e4*t4
t5 ~~ e5*t5
pulse =~ 0*t0 + 1*t1 + 0.51*t2 + 0.15*t3 + 0.04*t4
slope =~ 0*t0 + 2*t1 + 3*t2 + 4*t3 + 5*t4 + 6*t5
intercept =~ 1*t0 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4 + 1*t5
"
fit <- growth(mod, data=simdat)
summary(fit, fit.measures=T)

the problem seems to arise from the residual variance estimation from 't1'. rerunning the simulation with different seeds, increasing sample size or adding noise to the indicators did not help.

does anyone have a clue? any help would be really much appreciated.
thank you in advance and regards
robert

> t0 <- init + pulse*0.00 + decay*0

> t2 <- init + pulse*0.51 + decay*3

> t5 <- init + pulse*0.00 + decay*6
> simdat <- data.frame(id,t0,t1,t2,t3,t4,t5)

The correlation matrix of these variables will show you that they are
highly correlated. As a result, the observed sample covariance matrix is
nearly singular, inevitably causing problems.

Yves.

> Dear Yves,

> thank you for your response. this was also my first guess and in
> consequence i added noise to all indicators. however, even with low
> intercorrelations (and a large sample) lavaan still fails to recover the
> parameters.

But are you sure that the (lavaan) model that you are fitting, matches
the model that generated the data?

Perhaps, go the other way: specify a population model using lavaan
syntax, fixing all the parameters. Then, use simulateData() to generate
data according to this model. Then, fit the same model (but with free
parameters). You should be able to recover the parameters (with a
reasonable sample size). Finally, compare the data generated by
simulateData() to your manually generated data...

Yves.
